newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - May 6.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- A new television ad campaign for Tetra Pak-Grafobal, a producer of milk and fruit juices, features singer Bara Basikova in 30-second spots on CT 1 and TV Nova. The ads were created by Monte Cristo. (Strategie News, April 23-30)

-- Czech daily newspaper Blesk announces a new creative contest for the best full-page advertisement. The contest winner will get 10 free advertising pages in Blesk worth more than one million crowns ($32,400). Newspaper readers may enter the contest by responding to a survey on advertising. (Strategie News, April 23-30)

-- Advertising agency Enro RSCG Praha will host its second annual showing of some of the world's best television advertising on May 23 and 24 at its Noci Reklamozroutu (Nights of the Ad Munchers). Viewers will see 400 of the best TV ads from 47 countries. The event will be sponsored by Absolut Vodka. (Strategie News, April 23-30)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Czech Prima Television says IPB Banka wants to sell its 66 percent interest in Prima. Among the candidates so far are Scandinavian Broadcasting Systems, which is part of Walt Disney Co.'s ABC media group, and Prague's Nova television station. (Strategie News, April 23-30)
-- The Catholic daily publication Slowo-Dziennik Katolicki has ceased publishing since a planned takeover by a church foundation fell through. (Rzeczpospolita, 24 April,1997)
-- Czech public television devoted more time to last year's parliamentary elections than commercial television stations did. (Lidove Noviny, April 29)

-- The general director of the Czech Republic's Ceska Televize has complained by letter to the Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting about the general director of Nova Television. Ceska Televize's Ivo Mathe said Nova's Vladimir Zelezny is painting a picture for Nova viewers that Ceska Televize is a squanderous institution, ripping off viewers beyond control. (Pravo, April 30)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

-- Finnish-Polish confectionery maker Fazer is planning to double output this year and build a new plant in Poland, the company's president says. Fazer has a five percent share in the country's confectionery market. (Rzeczpospolita, 25 April 1997)

-- The Czech Republic's two favourite brands of potato chips are Bohemia Chips, favoured by 36 percent of Czech's, and Chio Chips, favoured by 20 percent, according to a survey out of Asia. (Strategie News, April 23-30)
-- Optical chain Vision Express says sales in Poland reached 24 million zlotys ($7.6 million) in 1996 and will double to 50 million zlotys this year.(Rzeczpospolita, 25 April 1997)

-- The Czech Republic's Radegast brewery is increasing prices for most of its of beers by between seven and nine percent. Radegast group, which includes the Velke Popovice and Radegast Sedlec breweries, is the second largest brewing group in the Czech Republic and controls 15.4 percent of the market. (Pravo, April 29)
--Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) has launched daily flights on the Copenhagen-Szczecin route. (Rzeczpospolita, 29 April 1997)

-- Prague's first Folli Follie boutique has opened in the city's Pavilon mall. Gerani, the Greek company's licensee in the Czech Republic, opened the shop. Another Folli Follie shop should open in the city centre later this year. (Strategie News, April 23-30)
CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Vodka is Poland's preferred alcoholic beverage, with 73.3 percent of adult Poles buying alcohol choosing clear quality vodkas, according to a survey from market research company Indicator. Premium Vodka, produced by the Polmos Zielona Gora distillery in western Poland, is the country's best-selling vodka. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, April 30, 1997)
--- About 20 percent of Poles have never dealt with a bank, a survey by the Pentor polling institute says. (Rzeczpospolita, 25 April 1997)
